subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server TCP and Unix WebSocket upgrades fail after a fixed 30-second handshake wait?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but choosing an unconditional cutoff changes runtime availability semantics for every configured Codex WebSocket endpoint and is an intentional maintainer-owned tradeoff.

options.title: Approve the 30-second bound
options.body: Land the shared transport timeout because a completed WebSocket upgrade should occur well within 30 seconds and indefinite waits are worse.

options.title: Choose another bounded value
options.body: Request a different fixed timeout if maintainers have evidence that supported proxies or Unix startup paths can legitimately require longer than 30 seconds.

recommendation.title: Approve the 30-second bound
recommendation.body: Land the shared transport timeout because a completed WebSocket upgrade should occur well within 30 seconds and indefinite waits are worse.

likelyOwner.reason: The original transport merger is the best available history-based owner for confirming its connection-failure semantics.
